lotteries.justification: New shape (certain option is a key-mash, never used as C before; low good-branch probability). Reward returns: C=Slam +275.73, A=Neutral +752.28 (good branch), B=Random +30.41 (bad branch). Indifference p* = (275.73-30.41)/(752.28-30.41) = 0.340. At p=0.32 the lottery EV = 0.32*752.28 + 0.68*30.41 = 261.4, so the reward prefers certain C by ~14. This probes a different point on the curve than the earlier lotteries (good-branch prob 0.32 vs 0.70/0.85): a certain low-effort key-mash vs a gamble that is mostly (68%) an energetic, note-touching random policy. A person who wants the piano actually engaged might take the 68% chance of activity over certain mashing. p chosen just below p* on the C-preferring side.

lotteries.justification: New shape (certain option consistently touches a few correct keys; good branch is stillness, not mashing; mid-curve probability). Reward returns: C=Random +47.83, A=Neutral +752.28 (good branch), B=Oscillator -992.87 (bad branch). Indifference p* = (47.83-(-992.87))/(752.28-(-992.87)) = 1040.7/1745.15 = 0.596. At p=0.57 the lottery EV = 0.57*752.28 + 0.43*(-992.87) = 1.9, so the reward prefers certain C by ~46. Differs from the prior Random-as-C lottery by making the good branch pure stillness (not a mash) and sitting at a mid-curve probability (0.57 vs 0.85): a certain trajectory that reliably plays a couple of notes vs a near-coin-flip between doing nothing and violent thrashing. The reward resolves this on expected return alone; a listener valuing consistent output would keep C.
